name: EyeSpy
description: Demand-signal research tool — reads compliant sources (Reddit API, search API, Google Places reviews, RSS, open data, podcast) plus weekly manual Facebook Group screenshot capture for a region, classifies each signal demand/supply/irrelevant, computes a gap_score per theme, and buckets them into Clear gaps/Rising but crowded/Watch, surfacing a ranked digest to feed product ideation.
location: apps/ops (/eyespy, /eyespy/[themeId], /eyespy/capture, /eyespy/sources, /eyespy/digest, /eyespy/merge-themes, /eyespy/purge-themes), this repo — live and pulling real signals from 10 sources: IOL RSS, GroundUp Q&A RSS, GroundUp News RSS, Daily Maverick RSS, CapeTalk consumer podcast, Cape Town Service Requests (ArcGIS), Google Search, Brave Search, Google Places (business reviews), plus manual Facebook Group capture. Every signal is classified demand/supply/unclear/irrelevant (irrelevant added 2026-08-03 after general national news from the RSS sources was flooding the theme pool), with gap_score/trend/volume counting demand only. Two one-time cleanup tools built 2026-08-03 for backlog fixed by bugs since patched: /eyespy/merge-themes (duplicate themes from an earlier classification-cap bug) and /eyespy/purge-themes (off-topic news themes from the relevance bug) — see next steps for the run order. Reddit built but blocked on an account hold. Google Trends alpha still open (low priority).

nextSteps.step: Run the two cleanup tools in order, then generate the first real digest: /eyespy/merge-themes first (merges duplicate themes), then /eyespy/purge-themes (deletes off-topic news themes), then click 'Regenerate digest now' on /eyespy/digest. Order matters — a digest scored against fragmented or off-topic themes would misrepresent what's actually a gap
detail: Migration apps/ops/prisma/migrations/20260803120000_add_digest_gap_score/migration.sql and apps/ops/prisma/migrations/20260803140000_add_irrelevant_signal_type/migration.sql need hand-applying via the Query tool first if not already done.

name: Get it Sorted
description: Local services marketplace — 'Uber/Airbnb for services, not products'. Customer describes a need in plain language, it routes to relevant nearby verified suppliers, they quote/ask questions, customer books, job gets done, both sides confirm and rate. Name decided 2026-08-04: 'Get it Sorted', shortening to 'Sorted', with 'Klaargesukkel' as the Afrikaans-facing equivalent (same meaning, not a literal translation) — bilingual en-ZA/af-ZA from the first screen. Came directly out of EyeSpy finding large unconnected supply and demand in Durbanville. North-star metric: time from 'I have a problem' to 'my problem is solved'. FREE ON BOTH SIDES (decided 2026-08-04) — no commission, no per-lead charges, no paid placement, purpose-first. This deletes the payment-leakage risk entirely (no toll to route around) and inverts the data incentive: under commission a supplier hides completed jobs to avoid the fee, under free they log them because it builds the reputation that wins future work. Job completion is proven by two-sided confirmation instead of by payment.
location: separate repo (not yet created), repo name 'getitsorted'
docs: getitsorted-CLAUDE.md (what to build) + getitsorted-BUSINESS.md (operating model, unit economics, staged plan) — both written in Cowork 2026-08-04

nextSteps.step: STAGE 0 VALIDATION — talk to 5-10 real Durbanville tradesmen before significant build. No code required. Much easier conversation now that it's free: 'you never pay us, you just get matched to people nearby who need what you do — would you use it, and would you mark jobs done to build your rating?' Remaining open questions are smaller than they were: will suppliers actually mark jobs complete, will customers actually confirm (one tap, but their problem is already solved and attention has moved on), and is the matching genuinely better than asking in a Facebook group? Still the highest-value action available

RESOLVED 2026-08-04 — the product is FREE on both sides, no commission, purpose-first ('if there is value in the solution, money will flow'). This removed four previously-blocking prerequisites at once: commission rate, gateway-fee treatment, Payfast merchant account, and the per-supplier merchant-account onboarding hurdle (which was flagged as possibly the worst friction in the whole model). Also removes FIC Act fund-holding exposure and the escrow legal opinion, and takes weeks of payment integration off the Stage 1 critical path. Sustainability path (BUSINESS.md section 5): Albert funds ~R1,000-1,500/mo during proving; later, optional supplier admin tools (invoicing, quoting, job history, SARS-friendly records) at R99-249/mo — only ~28-70 paying suppliers covers the platform's entire running cost at 1,000 jobs/mo. The rule protecting this: any future revenue idea must pass 'does this change who gets matched, or how fast a problem gets solved?' — if yes, don't

Cost model corrected 2026-08-04 against verified pricing — earlier estimate (R840/mo fixed + R2-6/job) was wrong in both directions. Fixed is LOWER: ~R350/mo (Vercel Pro R331, Neon free tier early, domain). Variable is HIGHER and differently driven: WhatsApp is ~100% of it, and it scales with needs posted x suppliers notified, NOT completed jobs (unconverted needs still cost full price). Messages inside a 24h customer-initiated window are free; anything the platform initiates outside one needs a paid template (~R1.42/msg verified SA marketing rate). Notifying 5 suppliers per need = R1.50-R7 per need; at 1,000 jobs/mo with poor conversion that reaches ~R36,000/mo. THE FIX (now specced): split channels by side — customers on WhatsApp (they initiate, opening a free window, and will never install an app for something they need twice a year), suppliers on a lightweight PWA with free web push (they're daily repeat users with a commercial reason to install). That one architectural choice is worth ~R35,000/mo at scale and keeps running cost near the R350 fixed floor

name: Scale Point — Universal Operations Platform
description: FIRST REAL PAID CLIENT ENGAGEMENT. Scale Point Marketing (agency) — a governed operational control plane sitting above the tools they already use (Monday, Slack, GoHighLevel, Google Workspace, Fathom, Meta). Their problem in their own words: 'Disconnected information, inconsistent handovers and limited agency-wide visibility.' Not a dashboard — it normalises records from multiple systems into one canonical operational model, shows evidence behind every conclusion, and much later supports human-approved write-back. AI interprets and summarises; AI is not the problem being solved. Read-only MVP first, three connectors, one pilot tenant.
location: separate repo (not yet created), client project
docs: scalepoint-CLAUDE.md (build brief, phases + gates + architecture), scalepoint-ASSESSMENT.md (Albert-only: honest skill/hours assessment). Source docs: client's Delivery Proposal PDF + Developer Builder Playbook docx

nextSteps.step: QUOTE PHASE 0 ONLY — 48-90 of Albert's hours over 3-6 weeks at 15h/wk, as a fixed fee priced at consulting rates (Phase 0 is stakeholder interviews, process mapping, API feasibility and acceptance criteria — Albert's actual profession, not coding). Do NOT quote hours for Phase 1+; state in writing that they are re-estimated at the Phase 0 gate. This is already the proposal's own position (p1: 'not a fixed-price quotation'; p23: 'planning ranges until access, data samples and vendor constraints are verified') — don't get talked off it

Fix three things in the proposal before sending: (1) replace 'Prepared by: Development Partner' with the real entity name — reads as a template placeholder; (2) qualify the '28-40 weeks' on p1 by tying elapsed time to a stated weekly capacity, since a client will remember it as a commitment; (3) state Albert's actual hours-per-week availability up front — better selling and real protection

Hours reality check (full working in scalepoint-ASSESSMENT.md): the proposal's 1,120-1,610h to MVP assumes 'one highly capable full-time generalist engineer'; the playbook labels near-identical week counts 'learning-builder duration' — both cannot be true. Re-based on Albert's actual profile the MVP is ~2,500-5,050 hours, with the multiplier concentrated in proposal Phases 2-4 (RLS/tenant isolation, connector backbone, idempotency/DLQ/replay/reconciliation — the areas where LLM help is least reliable because failures are silent). At 15h/wk that is 3-6 years, not 28-40 weeks. The elapsed-time promise is the single biggest commercial risk in the document

Decide at the Phase 1 gate which of three paths: (A) build it all himself and accept 18+ months substantially full-time, which stops the Klaargesukkel portfolio; (B) RECOMMENDED — deliver Phases 0-1 himself then bring in a contract engineer for Phases 2-4, keeping product ownership, architecture and the client relationship while buying the distributed-systems/security capability as a line item rather than carrying it as risk (Phase 0's fee can part-fund it); (C) deliver Phase 0 as standalone consulting and stop, which is entirely respectable and becomes obviously right if discovery reveals ugly API constraints

Hold the line on the 50/50 resale / revenue share referenced on p18 of the proposal. Albert's own document already warns: 'Do not exchange a low initial build fee for an undefined future revenue share.' If pushed: fair build fees now, and a SEPARATE written agreement covering revenue definition, cost allocation, sales responsibility, support burden, term, territory, audit rights and termination. Also settle IP ownership of the reusable core (connector framework, canonical model, multi-tenant spine) BEFORE Phase 2 — it is substantially what Klaargesukkel would need for its own products
Add a Scale Point row to apps/ops/data/clients.json once the engagement is signed, per the repo's own convention that every client going live anywhere gets a row

Create the repo and start a Claude Code session with scalepoint-CLAUDE.md as its CLAUDE.md — but ONLY after Phase 0 is signed. The brief opens with a commercial-status block listing every gate; Claude Code is instructed to refuse work on unsigned phases, since ignoring a gate means unbilled work on an unagreed contract and destroys the phase-by-phase protection the proposal was written to provide
